title: North Foundry kickoff
transcript:
[01:19] Syed Laeeq Ahmed: Welcome everyone. Today is about how we work together and which three clients we start with.
[02:12] Zainab Malik: I have the plan: Brightpath website first, then the Harborline portal, then the Tidewell app.
[03:14] Daniyal Chaudhry: Engineering will use two-week sprints and async standups in the engineering channel.
[03:42] Maya Hendricks: Each client gets a shared channel so they can ask questions without email chains.
[04:04] Elena Petrova: I will run sprint planning every second Monday and send a short client update on Fridays.
[04:56] Areeba Khan: Design can start wireframes for Brightpath this week if we get the sitemap by Wednesday.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Three launch clients: Brightpath, Harborline, Tidewell
• Two-week sprints, async standups
• One shared channel per client

✅ Decisions Made
• Sprints start on Mondays
• Friday client updates owned by Elena

📌 Action Items
• Elena: Send sitemap request to Brightpath
• Maya: Create shared client channels
• Daniyal: Set up the repositories

💡 Overall Summary
The team agreed on the launch order, sprint rhythm and communication channels with clients.

title: Brightpath discovery review
transcript:
[01:09] Elena Petrova: Thanks Rebecca for joining. We would like to confirm the sitemap and the booking flow.
[02:03] Rebecca Stone: Patients mostly book on their phones, so the booking request has to be very short.
[02:30] Areeba Khan: We can reduce it to name, phone, service and preferred time.
[03:21] Sana Iqbal: That also helps accessibility and keeps the form fast.
[03:50] Rebecca Stone: Perfect. We also want the team photos and a page for each service.
[04:33] Maya Hendricks: We will share the first wireframes in the channel by Tuesday.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Booking form is the main conversion goal
• Service pages for implants, whitening and braces
• Team photos needed from the client

✅ Decisions Made
• Four fields on the booking form
• Wireframes shared by Tuesday

📌 Action Items
• Areeba: Share homepage wireframes
• Rebecca: Send team photos
• Sana: Prototype the booking form

💡 Overall Summary
The client confirmed a short mobile-first booking form and a page for every service.

title: Sprint 2 review
transcript:
[01:00] Elena Petrova: Sprint 2 delivered visual design for Brightpath and the shipment API for Harborline.
[02:06] Bilal Qureshi: The shipment endpoints are on staging with pagination and filters.

[03:40] Hamza Rauf: I can start the service pages as soon as the design tokens are merged.

summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points

• Shipment API on staging
• Design tokens still to merge

✅ Decisions Made
• No new scope in sprint 3

📌 Action Items
• Hamza: Start service pages

💡 Overall Summary
Sprint 2 hit its goals. The team moves into build mode with no new scope.

title: Harborline requirements call
transcript:
[01:31] Maya Hendricks: Aaron, we want to confirm who can see what in the portal.
[02:29] Aaron Whitfield: Dispatchers need everything. Customers only see their own shipments and invoices.
[03:33] Omar Farooq: We can do that with customer accounts and a dispatcher role.
[04:07] Bilal Qureshi: Notifications by email first, SMS can follow if the budget allows.
[04:39] Aaron Whitfield: Email and SMS both, but SMS only for delivery day.
[05:14] Elena Petrova: I will update the estimate and send it tomorrow.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Two kinds of users: dispatchers and customers
• Email notifications for every status, SMS only on delivery day

✅ Decisions Made
• SMS limited to delivery day

📌 Action Items
• Elena: Send updated estimate
• Omar: Draft the role matrix
• Aaron: Share a sample invoice

💡 Overall Summary
Roles and notification rules for the Harborline portal were settled.

title: Brightpath launch go/no-go
transcript:
[01:19] Daniyal Chaudhry: Quick check before tonight's cutover. Usman, status?
[01:49] Usman Tariq: DNS is ready with a low TTL and a rollback plan written down.
[02:45] Kamran Ali: All 38 blog redirects are tested and the sitemap is ready to submit.
[03:09] Sana Iqbal: Accessibility pass is done and contrast issues are fixed.
[04:01] Rebecca Stone: We are happy to go ahead tonight.
[04:19] Daniyal Chaudhry: Go. Usman owns the cutover.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• DNS and rollback ready
• Redirects verified
• Accessibility fixed

✅ Decisions Made
• Launch tonight, Usman owns the cutover

📌 Action Items
• Usman: Run the DNS cutover
• Kamran: Submit sitemap after launch
• Elena: Message the client when live

💡 Overall Summary
Everything was ready and the Brightpath site was approved to go live that night.

title: Sales and outreach sync
transcript:
[01:24] Rania Haider: We have sent about 1,400 emails and booked 14 calls so far.
[02:29] Jordan Pierce: Clinics reply the most. Logistics companies need two follow-ups.
[03:39] Sofia Marin: I need a shorter proposal template. The current one is nine pages.
[04:32] Zainab Malik: Let's aim for three pages and a clear price table.
[05:07] Kamran Ali: I can add case study links so prospects can see the Brightpath results.
[06:11] Rania Haider: Good. Jordan will send the clinic list again next week.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Clinics reply the most
• Logistics needs more follow-ups
• Proposal template too long

✅ Decisions Made
• Proposal template cut to three pages

📌 Action Items
• Sofia: Shorten proposal template
• Kamran: Add case study links to emails
• Jordan: Resend the clinic list

💡 Overall Summary
Outreach is working best with clinics. The team will shorten proposals and add case studies.

title: Tidewell app design review
transcript:
[01:43] Areeba Khan: Nadia, here is the order flow from menu to checkout.
[02:15] Nadia El-Sayed: I love it. Can the loyalty card sit on the home screen?
[02:35] Tomas Alvarez: Yes, we can show stamps right under the greeting.
[03:10] Hamza Rauf: That is easy to build and keeps the checkout short.
[03:39] Nadia El-Sayed: Let's launch the beta in three weeks to our regulars.
[04:26] Sana Iqbal: We will prepare a TestFlight build before that.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Loyalty card on the home screen
• Beta for regular customers in three weeks

✅ Decisions Made
• Beta target: mid September

📌 Action Items
• Tomas: Update the home screen
• Sana: Build loyalty stamps
• Usman: Prepare TestFlight

💡 Overall Summary
The Tidewell design was approved with the loyalty card moved to the home screen.

title: Sprint 6 retro
transcript:
[00:59] Elena Petrova: What went well in sprint 6?
[02:03] Daniyal Chaudhry: Reviews were fast. Almost every PR was reviewed within a day.
[03:03] Hira Shahid: QA caught the push notification bug before the client saw it.
[03:46] Usman Tariq: Builds are now under three minutes after the cache change.
[04:46] Priya Nair: We underestimated the invoice PDFs. They took longer than planned.
[05:47] Elena Petrova: Let's pad the estimate on anything with documents or emails.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Reviews fast
• QA caught a notification bug early
• Builds under three minutes
• PDF work was underestimated

✅ Decisions Made
• Add buffer to estimates with documents or emails

📌 Action Items
• Elena: Update the estimate checklist
• Hira: Share the test plan template

💡 Overall Summary
A positive retro. The main lesson was to add buffer to document-heavy work.

title: Harborline phase 2 discussion
transcript:
[01:50] Sofia Marin: Aaron, the pilot has been running for four weeks. How is it going?
[02:22] Aaron Whitfield: Dispatchers love the tracking page. Customers ask about proof-of-delivery photos.
[03:13] Bilal Qureshi: We can add photo upload for drivers and show it on the shipment page.
[04:04] Aaron Whitfield: Great. And can we export a monthly report?
[04:54] Elena Petrova: We can scope both as phase 2 and send an estimate.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Pilot going well
• Proof-of-delivery photos requested
• Monthly report export requested

✅ Decisions Made
• Scope photos and reports as phase 2

📌 Action Items
• Elena: Send phase 2 estimate
• Bilal: Spike photo upload
• Sofia: Book the follow-up call

💡 Overall Summary
Harborline wants proof-of-delivery photos and monthly reports, both scoped as phase 2.

title: WebflowX product planning
transcript:
[01:43] Syed Laeeq Ahmed: We ship fast, but first load and page switches still feel slower than they should.
[02:36] Hamza Rauf: I can preload the next page and cache the workspace data on the client.
[03:42] Noor Fatima: Meeting summaries are solid. The next win is turning action items into tasks.
[04:20] Priya Nair: Importers for Slack and Notion would remove the biggest switching barrier.
[04:52] Daniyal Chaudhry: I would also publish a security page and plan single sign-on.
[05:19] Syed Laeeq Ahmed: Order: speed first, action items to tasks second, importers third.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• Speed is priority one
• Action items to tasks is a clear product win
• Importers reduce switching cost

✅ Decisions Made
• Priority order: speed, action items, importers

📌 Action Items
• Hamza: Finish preload and client cache
• Noor: Prototype action items to tasks
• Priya: Scope the Slack importer

💡 Overall Summary
The team set the WebflowX priorities for Q4: speed, action items to tasks, then importers.

title: Tidewell beta feedback
transcript:
[01:07] Hira Shahid: We had 46 testers and 31 pieces of feedback. Most are small.
[01:29] Nadia El-Sayed: Customers want to reorder their last drink with one tap.
[02:18] Hamza Rauf: That is a quick win. We can save the last order locally.
[03:03] Omar Farooq: Payments worked well. We had two declined cards, both expected.
[04:05] Priya Nair: Push notifications arrive in under five seconds.
summary:
📋 Meeting Summary

🎯 Key Points
• 46 testers, 31 feedback items
• Reorder last drink requested
• Payments and push notifications stable

✅ Decisions Made
• Add one-tap reorder before store submission

📌 Action Items
• Hamza: Build one-tap reorder
• Hira: Retest payments on iOS 17 and 18
• Nadia: Invite 20 more testers

💡 Overall Summary
The Tidewell beta is healthy. One-tap reorder is the main addition before store submission.

title: Q4 planning
transcript:

[02:20] Rania Haider: The pipeline has 24 open leads and 5 proposals out.

summary:

• 24 open leads, 5 proposals out
• Three clients on care plans
• Hiring two engineers

✅ Decisions Made
• Q4: two new clients and the Tidewell launch
• Protect WebflowX focus time

📌 Action Items
• Elena: Draft the Q4 roadmap
• Zainab: Open the two engineer roles
• Rania: Prepare the pipeline report

Q4 goals were set around new clients, the Tidewell launch and protecting product time.
